chunks: We did not find many of them faithful to their promises, and found many of them disobedient.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the faithfulness of the Children of Israel to their covenants?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-A'raf (7:101) is often interpreted as a critique of the majority of the Children of Israel who, despite receiving clear signs, frequently broke their covenants with God, displaying a disposition of fasq (transgression). This historical pattern serves as a cautionary tale for the Ummah, illustrating how numerical majority does not guarantee spiritual correctness, a theme resonating with the concept of the 'majority' (akthar) in contrast to the 'few' who remain steadfast. The verse underscores the fragility of divine covenants when not upheld by sincere faith and obedience.
